name: Iaculo Swarm
body:
Iaculo Swarm
CR 8

XP 4,800
N Tiny animal (swarm)
Init +6; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +11

DEFENSE

AC 21, touch 16, flat-footed 17 (+3 Dex, +1 dodge, +5 natural, +2 size)
hp 102 (12d8+48)
Fort +11, Ref +11, Will +7
Defensive Abilities swarm traits

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., climb 30 ft.
Melee swarm (2d6)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 0 ft.
Special Attacks puncture

STATISTICS

Str 7, Dex 16, Con 17, Int 2, Wis 12, Cha 5
Base Atk +9; CMB +11 (+15 with grapple); CMD 19
Feats Agile Maneuvers, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Skill Focus (Perception), Toughness
Skills Climb +22, Perception +11, Stealth +22; Racial Modifiers +4 Climb, +4 Stealth

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Puncture (Ex)

If a creature leaves a iaculo swarm’s square, the swarm takes 1d4 points of damage to reflect the loss of its numbers as several iaculi stay stuck into the victim’s flesh. A creature riddled with iaculi takes swarm damage at the end of its turn each round and has its speed halved by the javelin snakes stabbed through its limbs. As a full round action, the creature can remove the snakes with a DC 19 Fortitude save but takes swarm damage in doing so. At least 10 points of damage from any area effect destroy all the iaculi stuck into a creature.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate forests
Organization solitary or rain (1-6 swarms)
Treasure none

Iaculi form swarms within pristine, uninhabited forests.

They are not very social creatures, and so rarely attack all together unless the colony is somehow menaced or the iaculi are controlled by an external force.

Traveling alone is always a concern, you just never know what you’re going to be accosted by; bandits, spurned lovers, jealous husbands, monsters of the night – and the day come to think of it. Though traveling with others, especially merchant caravans, are particularly dangerous. You would think that with all that armor, wheeled shelter and men-at-arms, one would be safe.

No, no, no. If anything, you are more of a target; all that rattling noise, so easy to pinpoint in the vastness of the poorly patrolled forest pathway. I told the caravan master not to come this way, but who listens to world weary Troubadour? Certainly not this fool.

The first scream from the forward guards reached us and I knew we were in trouble. What would it be this time? Bears, forest cats or something more magical in nature.

I was surprised to see the guard come running back riddled with colorful arrows, but they were wriggling about. Others were helping get these projectiles out of his flesh and to my horror, those that were pulled out, tried to slither back into the undergrowth. I watched one of these frightful escapees reach a nearby tree and, with supernatural speed, ascend into the canopy, no doubt to try and use me as its new target.
